assessments.reasoning: I retrieved Oracle's governing Java SE 21 JLS from its edition-specific HTTPS locator and matched the frozen source SHA-256 before inspecting every listed paragraph. JLS §14.20.1 keys selection to the thrown value's run-time type and the catchable classes. It chooses the first assignment-compatible catch clause from the left and executes that clause. The frozen conditions identify this exact case of ordinary try-catch. The targeted comparison found no applicable contradiction.

challenge.method: Check overlapping valid subtype and supertype handlers, an earlier incompatible handler, a multi-catch alternative, no match, a throw from the selected handler, a non-throw abrupt completion, and the separate finally and resource forms.
challenge.results: A valid subtype handler comes first when both it and a later supertype handler match. An earlier incompatible clause is skipped. A matching alternative locates its enclosing multi-catch clause. An unmatched throw escapes, a handler throw follows that handler's completion rule, and a return or break selects no handler. Under §14.20.2, finally can replace a pending completion. Under §14.20.3.2, an extended resource form can also catch initialization and closing failures. These cases respect the claim's boundaries.

limitations: This covers handler selection for a throw from the try block of an ordinary try-catch statement. Completion of the selected handler and resource or finally forms have separate rules.
